chat.title: Rollcfluence help
chat.greeting: Hi, great to see you! I'm the Rollcfluence helper. Ask me anything about Shield, or pick a question below.
chat.followUp: Anything else I can help with?
chat.hello: Hello! Lovely to meet you. What would you like to know about keeping your AI keys safe?
chat.thanksReply: You're very welcome! I'm here whenever you need me.
chat.suggestions.0: How much latency does it add?
chat.noMatch: That's a great one, and it deserves a proper answer from the team. Leave your email and we'll reply to you personally.
chat.thanks: Thank you! Your question is with the team and we'll email you back soon.
chat.extra.0.a: Starter is free for 10k protected requests a month. Pro is €49 a month for 200k, Team is €299 for 1.25M, Scale is €799 for 3.5M, and Business is custom. Your AI provider bills its own usage separately.
chat.extra.1.a: Leave your email in the early access form at the bottom of the page. Keys go out in small batches.
chat.extra.2.a: Email rollcfluence@gmail.com, or leave your question here with your email.
chat.extra.3.a: Shield is a firewall for your AI API keys. Your OpenAI, Anthropic or other provider key stays in our encrypted vault, and your app gets a Shield key with a spend cap, a rate limit and filters built in. A leaked Shield key can only spend what you allow.
chat.extra.4.a: Pick by monthly requests: Starter (free) up to 10k, Pro (€49) up to 200k, Team (€299) up to 1.25M, Scale (€799) up to 3.5M, and Business above that. The Shield check after sign-up also recommends a plan from your answers.
chat.extra.5.a: Yes. Starter is free forever for 10k protected requests a month and 2 gateway keys, with spend caps, rate limits, the injection filter and auto-lock included. No card needed.
chat.extra.6.a: No. Prices are in euros per month, excluding VAT. VAT is added where it applies.
chat.extra.7.a: Yes. Plans renew monthly and you can cancel from Plan and billing in your dashboard. You keep your plan until the end of the period you paid for, then move back to Starter.
chat.extra.8.a: By card, through a certified card processor. We never see or store your card number. Business plans can be invoiced.
chat.extra.9.q: What happens when I go over my plan?
chat.extra.9.a: When the monthly request allowance is used up, Shield stops forwarding new requests until the next month or until you move to a bigger plan. There are no surprise overage charges.
chat.extra.10.a: Each Shield key has a daily and a monthly cap in dollars. Shield adds up the estimated cost of every request, and once a cap is reached it answers with an error and never calls your provider, so the bill stops there.
chat.extra.11.q: What if my Shield key leaks?
chat.extra.11.a: A leaked Shield key can only spend up to its cap, at its rate limit, from the IPs and countries you allow. You can revoke or lock it in one click, auto-lock can shut it off when attacks repeat, and your real provider key is never exposed.
chat.extra.12.a: Spend caps, rate limits, a model allow-list, an IP allow-list, country blocking, key expiry, a max output tokens ceiling, a prompt-injection filter, PII masking, auto-lock, alerts and a security log. Bot traps and provider failover are coming next.
chat.extra.13.q: Does the injection filter stop every attack?
chat.extra.13.a: No filter can promise that. Ours catches common jailbreak and prompt-leak phrases with patterns today. Treat it as one layer next to caps, rate limits and allow-lists, which are hard limits.
chat.extra.14.a: When it is on, emails, card numbers and phone numbers in prompts are replaced before the request leaves for the provider. It is available on Pro and above.
chat.extra.15.a: Account data is stored in an EU database in Frankfurt. Prompts and responses are not stored at all. Request details are kept for up to 90 days. The Privacy policy and DPA have the full detail.
chat.extra.16.a: We built Shield for EU teams: prompts are not stored, account data sits in the EU, request history is kept for up to 90 days, and a Data Processing Agreement is published at /dpa. We do not claim any certification we do not have.
chat.extra.17.a: They are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before they are saved, and no endpoint ever returns them, not even to you. Only the gateway decrypts a key in memory to forward your request.
chat.extra.18.q: How do I set it up?
chat.extra.18.a: Sign in, add your provider key, create a Shield key, then change two lines in your app: the base URL to https://rollcfluence-shield.vercel.app/v1 and the API key to your Shield key. Your existing SDK keeps working.
chat.extra.19.q: Can I use Gemini, Mistral or other models?
chat.extra.19.a: Yes, any provider with an OpenAI-compatible chat API works through /v1/compat: Google Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, xAI, OpenRouter, Together, Fireworks and more. Add the provider under Provider keys in the dashboard.
chat.extra.20.a: Yes. Streaming responses pass through chunk by chunk on every supported provider, and usage is still counted.
chat.extra.21.q: Can I try the dashboard first?
chat.extra.21.a: Yes. Open the demo at /app?demo to click through a dashboard filled with sample data. Nothing you do there is saved.
chat.extra.22.a: Nine quick questions when you sign up. You get a risk score, what to fix first, a recommended plan and a setup list that ticks itself off as you configure Shield.
chat.extra.23.a: Yes. Shield can alert you by email, Slack, Discord or a signed webhook when requests are blocked, a cap is close, or a key gets locked.
chat.extra.24.q: Can I limit each of my own users?
chat.extra.24.a: You can send your end user ID with each request and see who spends what in the Live view. Hard per-user limits for your customers are coming next on the Team plan.
chat.extra.25.q: Do you have team seats or SSO?
chat.extra.25.a: Not yet. Roles for up to 10 seats are coming next on Team, and SSO with unlimited seats is planned for Business.
chat.extra.26.a: Provider failover, bot traps, per-user limits for your customers, team roles, smarter injection detection, native Cohere, Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock, and an EU-only region.
chat.extra.27.a: We open Shield to 100 teams per batch, so every team gets set up properly and every key is watched closely. Confirm your email on the waitlist to hold your spot.
chat.extra.28.a: Small teams and startups that call AI APIs from their product and cannot afford a leaked key or a runaway bill, especially teams in the EU.
chat.extra.29.q: Why not just use the provider’s own limits?
chat.extra.29.a: Provider limits are per account and often only warn you after the money is spent. Shield gives every app and environment its own key with hard caps, rate limits, IP and country rules, and one place to revoke it, across all your providers.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: Before you switch your base URL.
faq.items.0.q: Do I need to change my code?
faq.items.0.a: Only the base URL and the key. Shield speaks the same API as the provider you already use, so your SDK keeps working.
faq.items.1.q: How much latency does it add?
faq.items.1.a: We have not measured it on real traffic yet, so we will not quote a number. Shield is one extra hop, and streaming responses are passed through chunk by chunk.
faq.items.2.a: No. Shield does not store prompts or responses. It keeps only request details: time, key, model, token counts, estimated cost and whether it was blocked.
faq.items.3.q: What happens if Shield goes down?
faq.items.3.a: Requests through Shield fail with a clear error, so your app can fall back to calling the provider directly. A per-key fail-open switch is on our list, not built yet.
faq.items.4.a: OpenAI (/v1/chat/completions), Anthropic (/v1/messages) and any provider with an OpenAI-compatible chat API (/v1/compat/chat/completions), such as Google Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek, xAI or OpenRouter. Streaming works on all of them. Native Cohere, Azure OpenAI and AWS Bedrock are coming next.
faq.items.5.q: Can I bring my own keys?
faq.items.5.a: Yes. You add your OpenAI or Anthropic key once. It is stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM), and Shield issues gateway keys on top of it.

library.papers.0.title: Stolen Gemini API key runs up an $82,314 bill
library.papers.0.claim: charged in about two days on a stolen Google Cloud key, for a startup that normally spent around $180 a month.
library.papers.0.caveat: One reported case. It shows the scale, not a typical loss.
library.papers.1.title: LLMjacking: stolen cloud credentials used in new AI attack
library.papers.1.claim: is Sysdig's estimate of what an attacker can burn on a victim's account by reselling access to stolen AI keys.
library.papers.1.caveat: A worst-case estimate for a fully abused account, not an average.
library.papers.2.title: The State of Secrets Sprawl 2026
library.papers.2.claim: for AI services were found leaked on public GitHub in 2025, up 81% on the year before.
library.papers.2.caveat: Counts public GitHub only; private leaks are not included.
library.papers.3.title: Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025
library.papers.3.claim: is the global average cost of a data breach, from 600 organisations in 16 countries. The US average hit a record $10.22M.
library.papers.3.caveat: Covers all breaches, not only leaked AI keys.
library.papers.4.title: Data Breach Investigations Report 2025
library.papers.4.claim: of breaches started with stolen or abused credentials, the most common way attackers got in.
library.papers.4.caveat: Figure as summarised by Aembit; credentials of all kinds, not only API keys.
library.papers.5.title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
library.papers.5.claim: lower cost while matching GPT-4 accuracy, by sending each query to the cheapest model that can answer it well.
library.papers.5.caveat: 98% was the best of three datasets; the other two saved 73% and 59%.
library.papers.6.title: RouteLLM: Learning to Route LLMs from Preference Data
library.papers.6.claim: cheaper in some settings without losing response quality, by routing easy prompts to a smaller model.
library.papers.6.caveat: The paper says "in certain cases"; savings depend on your traffic.
library.papers.7.title: GPT Semantic Cache: Reducing LLM Costs and Latency via Semantic Embedding Caching
library.papers.7.claim: fewer API calls by answering repeated, similar questions from a cache instead of the model.
library.papers.7.caveat: A preprint, not yet peer-reviewed. Works best when users ask similar things.
library.papers.8.title: LLMLingua: Compressing Prompts for Accelerated Inference of Large Language Models
library.papers.8.claim: shorter prompts with little loss in quality, so you pay for far fewer input tokens.
library.papers.8.caveat: At 20x Microsoft reports about a 1.5 point drop; results vary by task.
library.papers.9.title: Prompt caching with Claude
library.papers.9.claim: lower cost and up to 85% lower latency for long prompts that repeat, such as a big system prompt or document.
library.papers.9.caveat: Only the cached part of the prompt gets cheaper, and writing to the cache costs extra.
library.papers.10.title: Batch API
library.papers.10.claim: for requests that can wait: results come back within 24 hours at half the normal price.
library.papers.10.caveat: Not for live chat, and not every model supports it.

story.label: Why we started
story.title: AI keys became the most expensive passwords on the internet. Nobody was guarding them.
story.paragraphs.0: In three years, AI went from a demo to the engine inside millions of products. Every one of those products runs on an API key, and every key can spend real money the second it leaks. A leaked password locks you out. A leaked AI key sends you the bill.
story.paragraphs.1: Big companies answer this with security teams and custom gateways. Everyone else has a .env file and hope. The numbers show how that ends: 1.27 million AI keys leaked in one year, and attackers who turn a single stolen key into a $46,000 day.
story.paragraphs.2: We started Rollcfluence to close that gap. One key in your app, every model behind it, and limits that hold even when everything else goes wrong. The protection a large company would build for itself, ready for a solo developer in two lines of code.
threats.label: Threats
threats.title: Leaked keys are drained in minutes, not days.
threats.body: Bots scan every public commit and app bundle for strings that start with sk-. A key found at 02:00 can be resold and looped against GPT-4-class models before you wake up, and the invoice still has your name on it.
threats.items.0.name: Leaked keys
threats.items.0.text: Your real provider keys never leave our vault. Your app holds a scoped Rollcfluence key you can rotate or kill in one click.
threats.items.1.name: Prompt injection

threats.items.2.name: Bot and cost abuse
threats.items.2.text: Per-key rate limits and hard spend caps stop scripted traffic from turning into a five-figure invoice.

trust.title: Why you can trust us with your keys.
trust.items.0.name: Your keys are never shown back
trust.items.0.text: Provider keys are encrypted at rest. No endpoint returns them, not even to you.
trust.items.1.name: Leave in one line
trust.items.1.text: Shield speaks each provider's own API. Point your base URL back and you are out. No lock-in.
trust.items.2.name: If we go down, you are not stuck
trust.items.2.text: Requests fail with a clear error, so your app can call the provider directly. A per-key fail-open switch is coming next.
trust.items.3.name: Prompts are not kept
trust.items.3.text: Shield never stores prompts or responses. It logs only the request details you see in your dashboard.

vision.label: What comes next
vision.title: This is only the beginning.
vision.big.0: AI is moving from answering questions to taking actions. Agents already book, buy, write code and call other AIs on their own, and each of them holds a key. The more AI does, the more those keys are worth, to you and to anyone who steals them.
vision.big.1: Shield is our first step. The goal is bigger: to be the layer every company trusts to decide what its AI is allowed to spend and do. The teams in the first batches will shape what it becomes.
vision.cta: Claim a spot in the first batch
why.label: Why start now
why.title: Why teams start with Rollcfluence.
why.items.0.name: Live in minutes
why.items.0.text: Change two lines. Your SDK, your models and your prompts stay exactly as they are.
why.items.1.name: Costs capped from day one
why.items.1.text: Every key gets a hard daily limit, so the worst day is a number you chose in advance.
why.items.2.name: Every model, one key
why.items.2.text: OpenAI, Anthropic and any provider with an OpenAI-compatible API, like Gemini, Mistral, Groq, DeepSeek or xAI, behind keys you control.
why.items.3.name: Real people answer
why.items.3.text: Questions go straight to the team building Shield at rollcfluence@gmail.com.
